devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Four simple words carry enormous weight: "You shall not murder." Human life is precious to God because every person is made in His image (Gen 9:6). To take an innocent life is to attack something sacred — the image of the Creator stamped on a human being. This command guards the immense value God places on every person, from the strongest to the most fragile.

We may hear this and quietly feel we are safe; after all, most of us have never killed anyone. But Jesus took us deeper into the heart of this command. He taught that anger and contempt toward others are the roots from which murder grows (Matt 5:21-22). To nurse hatred, to write someone off, to wound with cutting words — all of this violates the spirit of this command. The issue is not only our hands but our hearts.

This turns the command from a low bar we easily clear into a mirror that exposes us all. Who among us has never harboured resentment or spoken to destroy? Here we run to Christ, who not only forgives our anger but pours His love into us so we can treat others as image-bearers of God. The gospel moves us from merely not killing to actively loving — even our enemies (Matt 5:44). Let God search your heart today for hidden anger, and hand it to Him.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Is there anger or contempt in my heart that I have been excusing?
- How does seeing every person as God's image-bearer change how I treat them?
- Who is God calling me to move toward with love instead of resentment?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, You value every life because every person bears Your image. Search my heart for hidden anger and bitterness, and fill me with Your love so that I honour others as You do. Amen.
